Conversation, family & daily routines

phew! interjection

relief

also what a relief, thank goodness that’s over, I can breathe again, all’s well

classical

Plaut. Ps. 1052: Hahae, nunc dēmum mī animus in tūtō est locō
Plaut. Truc. 209: Hahahae, requiēvī

Hahae!

phew! (joy and relief)

(vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

Lewis & Short (s.v. ha): “an exclamation of joy, thank heavens!”. Traupman gives ehem! for a phew of glad surprise or relief (p. 359).

Other words

  • 1respīrāvī: short e in re- (Lewis & Short rē-spīro). The lexicon’s ruling on re- before sc, sp, st (Bennett §48 rejects the lengthening for the lost d of red-). Still under review. Ruling: re- short before sc, sp, st.

    Respīrāvī.1 — I can breathe again

    perfect of respīrō; the present respīrō too · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 10.1.1: paulum respīrāvī; Cic. Att. 7.13.3: paulum respīrō

    Cicero’s word in the letters for relief after worry.

  • Salva rēs est. — all’s well, we’re safe

    also used · classical · Plaut. Aul. 207; Ter. Ad. 643; Traupman 270

    The words of relief after a fright.

  • Ehem! — ha! (glad surprise)

    also used · classical · Plaut. As. 2.4.43: ehem, optumē! quam dūdum tū advēnistī? (Lewis & Short); Traupman 359

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    Glad surprise at meeting someone or at good news, more than relief.

Examples

  • Hahae, nunc dēmum mī animus in tūtō est locō

    Phew, now at last my mind is in a safe placePlaut. Ps. 1052

  • Hahahae, requiēvī, quia intrō abiit odium meum.

    Phew, I can rest, now that my pest has gone in.Plaut. Truc. 209–210

  • accēpī litterās tuās et paulum respīrāvī

    I got your letter and breathed a little more freelyCic. Att. 10.1.1

  • Dī mē servant, salva rēs est.

    The gods are keeping me; all’s well.Plaut. Aul. 207

  • Ērubuit: salva rēs est.

    He blushed: all’s well.Ter. Ad. 643

See also let me catch my breath, thank God!, ha ha!.
